text.p: Public Service Enterprise Group Inc said the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities Wednesday approved a settlement addressing the cost impact of the shutdown of the Salem 1 and 2 nuclear units since the sprinq of 1995.
The company said the board also approved the settlement of the resolution of two other regulatory issues.
It also said final restart activities are underway for Salem 2, with fuel loading occurring this week and synchronization to the grid anticipated in February.
Public Service said refurbishment and replacement of steam generators continue at Salem 1, which is scheduled for restart in mid-1997.
The company said the settlements were reached in October by its utility subsidiary, Public Service Electric & Gas, the board's staff and the state's Ratepayer Advocate.

In its approval, the board included the requirement that PSE&G apply any potential net overcollection of energy costs that might exist on December 31, 1998, to stranded asset costs arising from any electric utility industry restructuring.

The settlements will result in an earnings loss of $62.3 million, or $0.26 per share of Public Service Enterprise Group common, the company said. Of the total, $0.25 per share was recorded in the third quarter of 1996 and the remaining $0.01 per share was recorded in 1995.
